patch.value: An approved generation budget the loop cannot advance past on its own

A loop that promotes its own successors has no natural stopping point, and the useful stopping rule is not a compute limit but a human decision recorded where the loop can read it. pm-rl binds a self-improvement programme to an approval item that states how many generations are authorized and on what evidence. Advancing beyond that count is refused, and the refusal names the approval item that must be extended, so the operator is told exactly what to write rather than which flag to add. This is the same shape as the release approval already governing which packages may publish: the gate is a tracked decision, not an environment variable, so it survives a fresh checkout, is reviewable in a diff, and cannot be satisfied by a process that merely sets something.

Advancing past the approved generation count exits non-zero and names the approval item to extend; extending the approval item permits exactly the additional generations it states; a programme with no approval item refuses at the first promotion rather than at the last; the budget is read from tracked project data and never from an environment variable

The approved number is interpreted as permitted promotions and never as a generation ordinal; the seed generation consumes no budget unit; a refused promotion consumes no unit and a subsequent successful promotion of the same candidate consumes exactly one; advancing past the approved count exits non-zero and names the approval item to extend; extending the approval item permits exactly the additional promotions it states; a programme with no approval item refuses at the first promotion rather than at the last; the budget is read from tracked project data and never from an environment variable

Advancing beyond that count is refused, and the refusal names the approval item that must be extended, so the operator is told exactly what to write rather than which flag to add. The counting boundary is part of the contract and not an implementation detail, because two readings of the same approval item would otherwise permit different numbers of successors. The approved number is a count of PERMITTED PROMOTIONS, not a maximum generation ordinal. The seed generation consumes no budget: it is not promoted, it is registered, and a programme that has only a seed has spent nothing. Each promotion of a candidate consumes exactly one unit at the moment it succeeds, so a refused promotion costs nothing and a retried candidate that then succeeds costs one. This is the same shape as the release approval already governing which packages may publish: the gate is a tracked decision, not an environment variable, so it survives a fresh checkout, is reviewable in a diff, and cannot be satisfied by a process that merely sets something.

value.text:
Corrective note: an earlier comment on this item describes countPromotedUnderApproval as SKIPPING a generation whose specification cannot be read. That was the behaviour when the comment was written and it is no longer true.

The shipped behaviour refuses. A generation with no JSON fence, or one whose spec fails to parse, makes the approved budget undecidable and the promotion is refused with budget_undecidable and exit code 4, naming the offending generation id and the reason. Treating unreadable provenance as absent provenance inverts the contract the budget exists to enforce, because the budget bounds a recursive loop that promotes programmatically and cannot notice a silently skipped record.

The budget guarantee this item delivers also changed twice after the item was first closed, so the current statement of it is: the promoted count and the promotion write are held in ONE workspace writer lock via commitWorkspaceTransaction; concurrent promotions serialize rather than one being refused for contention, so a loser re-reads the count the winner just changed and reports the accurate terminal budget_exceeded; and the already-promoted check is re-run INSIDE that lock, because the pre-lock check reads state every concurrent caller sees before any of them holds the lock, which let three concurrent promotions of one generation all succeed.

Recording this as an appended corrective entry rather than editing the original, so the sequence of what was believed when stays legible.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Second corrective note, tightening the first one. A reviewer pointed out that the previous entry stated the lock guarantee more strongly than the code delivers, and that is right.

The previous entry said concurrent promotions SERIALIZE rather than one being refused for contention. That is only true of callers that ACQUIRE the lock. The wait is BOUNDED, not unlimited: PROMOTION_LOCK_WAIT_MS is 30 seconds, and a caller that cannot acquire the lock within that window fails.

Verified empirically rather than reasoned about, by holding the lock in one process and attempting acquisition from another with a short wait. The loser throws with context code lock_conflict and exit code 4, and the message names the current owner and how long it waited, for example: Item sdk-workspace-transaction is locked (owner pA) after waiting 1204ms.

So the accurate statement of the guarantee is in two parts. Callers that acquire the lock serialize, and a loser re-reads the count the winner just changed and reports the terminal budget_exceeded. A caller that exceeds the bounded wait reports lock_conflict, which IS a retryable contention outcome. Contention is therefore BOUNDED rather than eliminated. What the design does guarantee is that contention is always REPORTED as contention, and never silently becomes a promotion that did not happen or one that exceeded the approved budget.

README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md carried the same overstatement and have been corrected in the same commit.

Noting the pattern honestly: this is the fifth documentation finding on this PR where prose asserted a mechanism more strongly than the implementation supports, and this one was in a note I wrote specifically to CORRECT an earlier inaccuracy.

patch.value: Approved generation budget shipped as a tracked-data gate: the count and the promoting write are atomic under a workspace writer lock, advancing past the approved count is refused and names the item to extend, the seed consumes no unit and each promotion consumes one.
test/lineage.test.ts passes the budget-refusal, distinct-candidate exhaustion, and concurrent-promotion cases; index.ts and lineage.ts at 100/100/100 lines/branches/functions; release:check green.

A loop that promotes its own successors cannot advance past the count a human authorized: the budget is a tracked Decision, advancing past it is refused and names the item to extend, the seed consumes no unit, each promotion consumes exactly one, and the count-plus-write is atomic under a workspace writer lock so concurrent promotions never exceed the approved count.

The approved promotion budget is read from tracked project data — a Decision approval item whose spec carries permitted_promotions — and never from an environment variable. Advancing past the approved count exits non-zero and names the approval item to extend; the seed generation consumes no unit and each successful promotion consumes exactly one (a refused promotion consumes none). As shipped, the count and the promoting write are serialized under one workspace writer lock via commitWorkspaceTransaction, so concurrent promotions cannot both read headroom and both proceed; a caller that exceeds the bounded PROMOTION_LOCK_WAIT_MS receives lock_conflict and re-reads nothing, and an in-lock re-check keeps one generation promoting at most once.
